ar-anime-rewatch: Some shows are built to be watched twice. The first time you're just trying to keep up with the plot. The second time you notice the background details, the lines that were obviously setting something up, the character who was lying the whole time.

Attack on Titan is the obvious one. Season one looks like a straightforward monster story until you know what's inside the walls, and then half the early dialogue reads completely differently. Frieren works the other way round: nothing is hidden, but the small flashback moments land much harder once you know how the journey ends.

Our other picks are Cowboy Bebop, Steins;Gate and Mob Psycho 100. None of them need a rewatch to be good, but all of them reward one. If you've only seen them once, pick one this weekend and watch the first episode again. You'll see what we mean.

Cowboy Bebop is a good example of a show that looks episodic until it isn't. On a first watch the bounty-of-the-week episodes feel like fun side stories, but a second time round you notice how often Spike's past with Vicious and Julia creeps in at the edges. Steins;Gate is even sneakier. Its opening episode is full of odd little moments that seem like throwaway weirdness, and nearly all of them turn out to matter once you know where Okabe's experiments lead.

Mob Psycho 100 rewards a rewatch for a different reason. Once you know how Mob's story with Reigen plays out, their early scenes together feel much warmer and a lot more complicated than the jokes suggest. A practical tip for any rewatch: switch off your phone and watch with subtitles even if you normally use a dub, because small wording choices often carry the clues. It also helps to leave a gap of a year or so, long enough to forget the details but not the ending.

Rewatching is also a nice way to share a show. Sitting down with a friend who is seeing it for the first time lets you enjoy their reactions while you quietly spot everything you missed, as long as you can keep a straight face. There is no rule that says a show has to be new to be worth your evening. Sometimes the best thing on your watchlist is something you have already finished.
ar-anime-openings: Streaming services put a Skip Intro button on everything, and anime fans mostly ignore it. That says a lot about how much work goes into a good opening sequence.

The best ones hide clues. Characters who haven't appeared yet show up in silhouette, colours shift when the story gets darker, and new cuts get swapped in mid-season once a spoiler is safe to show. Some studios even animate the OP after the whole season is finished so it can reflect the ending.

Then there's the music. A great opening song becomes the show's theme at concerts, in karaoke and all over edit videos for years. When a show goes quiet for its final episode and plays the OP over the last fight, that's the payoff for every week you didn't press skip.

Some openings have become bigger than the shows themselves. Cowboy Bebop's "Tank!", written by Yoko Kanno and played by her band Seatbelts, is a jazz number with no lyrics at all, and it still sets up the whole series in a couple of minutes. Neon Genesis Evangelion's "A Cruel Angel's Thesis" is a karaoke classic in Japan decades after it first aired. Linked Horizon's "Guren no Yumiya" from Attack on Titan turned "Sasageyo" into a phrase people shout at each other without ever having watched the show.

Newer openings have pushed the visual side even further. The Chainsaw Man opening, set to Kenshi Yonezu's "Kick Back", is packed with shots that recreate scenes from famous films, and fans spent weeks matching each one to its source. Jujutsu Kaisen's first opening, "Kaikai Kitan" by Eve, sneaks in hints about characters and fights that only make sense later. Oshi no Ko's "Idol" by YOASOBI went further still and became one of the biggest songs in Japan that year, pulling in listeners who had never seen an episode.

If you want to get more out of openings, look for the creditless versions that studios and streaming services often post on their official channels, because the animation is easier to read without names over the top. Rewatch the OP after you finish a season and you'll spot things you missed the first time. Most of all, give it a proper listen before you decide it's skippable. Ninety seconds a week is a small price for the moment it finally pays off.
ar-anime-seasonal: Anime in Japan mostly airs in four seasons, called cours, starting in January, April, July and October. Each one brings dozens of new shows, and most run for about twelve or thirteen episodes.

The trick is to not try to watch everything. Pick three or four shows after checking trailers and first episodes, then follow them weekly. Drop anything that isn't working after the third episode, which is usually when a show settles into its real tone.

Sequels are the easy wins because you already know you like them. For new titles, watch who's adapting it. A strong studio and a source manga or light novel with a good reputation are the two best signs a show will stay good all the way through.

Not every show fits neatly into one season. Some run for two cours in a row, which means about twenty-four episodes across six months, and others take a break in the middle and come back later as a split-cour. Frieren: Beyond Journey's End is a good example of a longer run, starting in autumn 2023 and carrying on into the new year. Then there are long-running shows like One Piece that air almost every week regardless of season, so they sit outside the calendar altogether.

A few tools make the whole thing much easier. Seasonal charts on sites like MyAnimeList and AniList list every new show with its studio, source material and airing day, and you can add titles to a personal list to track your progress. Most big shows are simulcast on streaming services within hours of airing in Japan, so check which platform has the rights in your country before you get attached. It is also worth muting a show's name on social media if you fall behind, because spoilers spread fast.

Keep in mind that there is no rush. Plenty of fans skip the weekly routine entirely and wait until a season has finished, then watch the ones everyone kept talking about. Studios like MAPPA, ufotable and Kyoto Animation have strong track records, but smaller studios surprise people every year too. Whether you follow ten shows or just one, the best season is the one you actually enjoy rather than the one you feel you should keep up with.
ar-gaming-openworld: For a while it felt like every big game had the same map: towers to climb, icons everywhere and a checklist that took eighty hours. It was busy, but it wasn't fun to explore.

Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom changed that. You look at a mountain, you go to the mountain, and something interesting is usually there. Elden Ring did the same thing with a darker tone, and hiding its best areas behind secrets made finding them feel like your own discovery.
The best open worlds give you a reason to wander instead of an order. If you finish a session and can't remember one thing you found by accident, the map probably isn't doing its job.

Other games have found their own ways to do this. Ghost of Tsushima replaced the usual waypoint marker with the Guiding Wind, which blows through the grass towards wherever you are heading, so you keep your eyes on the world rather than the minimap. Outer Wilds goes further still. Its solar system resets every twenty-two minutes, and the only thing you keep between loops is what you have learned, which turns exploring into genuine detective work.

If a big map feels overwhelming, you can often make it better yourself. Many games let you trim the HUD or turn off markers, and Assassin's Creed Odyssey even offers an Exploration mode that gives you directions instead of a pin on the map. Try ignoring side content for your first few hours and just following whatever catches your eye. Keeping a few notes on paper about places you want to come back to can feel surprisingly like being a real explorer.

None of this means big maps are bad. A huge world can be wonderful when the space between landmarks feels like it has a purpose, whether that is a view, a puzzle or a quiet moment on horseback. The games people remember years later are usually the ones where the most memorable thing that happened was not on any checklist. That is worth looking for the next time you pick a game to sink your weekends into.
ar-gaming-soulslike: Soulslikes have a reputation for being brutal, and they are, but they're also fair. Almost every death teaches you something about an enemy's timing or a room's layout.
Slow down. Walk into new areas with your shield up, learn one enemy at a time and don't be ashamed to go back and level up. Summons and spirit ashes aren't cheating. They're part of the design.
Most importantly, take breaks. The number of bosses that go down five minutes after coming back from a snack is honestly a bit suspicious.

Picking the right first game helps a lot. Elden Ring is a popular starting point because its open world means you can ride off on Torrent and explore somewhere else when a boss like Margit the Fell Omen is too much. Hollow Knight gives you the same learn-by-dying loop in 2D, which some players find easier to read. Sekiro is usually the one people suggest saving for later, since it takes away summons and builds almost everything around parrying, so you can't really grind your way past a wall like Genichiro.

A few habits make every Soulslike less painful. When you die, you drop your souls, runes or whatever the currency is called, so spend them before walking through a boss fog rather than carrying a fortune into a fight. Read the messages other players leave on the floor, although you should treat "try jumping" near a cliff with suspicion. In Bloodborne, attacking straight after taking a hit lets you win back some lost health, which is the game's way of telling you to be brave rather than hide.

It also helps to know that nobody finishes these games alone. The item descriptions are where most of the story lives, and a whole community of lore videos exists to piece it together, so don't worry if you finish a game with no idea what happened. Watching a guide for a boss you've been stuck on for an evening is fine too. Beating something that flattened you twenty times is the feeling these games are built around, and you earned it either way.
ar-gaming-indie: Indie games don't have huge budgets, so they have to win on ideas instead. That's why some of the most memorable games of the decade came from teams of fewer than twenty people.

Hades made roguelikes feel like a story you wanted to keep hearing. Hollow Knight built an entire sad, beautiful kingdom in hand-drawn art. Celeste turned a hard platformer into something about anxiety and self-acceptance.
Most of these are cheap, run on almost anything and can be finished in a few evenings. If you're burned out on sixty-hour epics, start here.

Some indies are made by tiny teams, and a few by one person. Eric Barone spent years building Stardew Valley on his own, handling the code, art and music himself. Toby Fox made most of Undertale solo, and its jokes and boss fights still get quoted by fans today. Outer Wilds, from Mobius Digital, is a space mystery where the only thing you carry forward between loops is your own knowledge, and Return of the Obra Dinn by Lucas Pope turns an insurance investigation into one of the cleverest detective games around.

Finding the good ones takes a bit of digging, but it is worth it. Steam Next Fest runs a few times a year and fills the store with free demos, so you can try dozens of upcoming games without spending anything. Wishlisting a game on Steam means you get an email when it goes on sale, and indies are discounted often. Subscription services like Game Pass also carry plenty of indie titles, and itch.io is full of short, experimental games made by students and hobbyists.

Indie games are also where a lot of ideas start before bigger studios borrow them. The deckbuilder boom owes a lot to Slay the Spire, and Vampire Survivors inspired a wave of copycats almost overnight. Supporting small developers, whether by buying their games, leaving a review or telling a friend, genuinely makes a difference to whether they get to make the next one. So pick something short and odd this weekend and see where it takes you.
ar-movies-trilogy: Sequels usually go wrong in one of two ways: they repeat the first film or they get so big that the characters disappear. The good sci-fi sequels avoid both.

Aliens switched genre from horror to action but kept Ripley at the centre. Blade Runner 2049 slowed down even more than the original and asked a new question about memory. Dune: Part Two widened the scale and made Paul's rise feel more like a warning than a victory.
The common thread is that each one knows what the first film was really about and pushes that idea further, instead of just adding more explosions.

Terminator 2: Judgment Day is another classic case. James Cameron took the unstoppable killer from the first film and made him a protector, which sounds like a gimmick but actually deepens the original's ideas about fate and whether the future can be changed. The Empire Strikes Back did something similar for Star Wars by letting the heroes lose, splitting them up and giving the story room to breathe before the final film.

It is also interesting how often good sci-fi sequels come from a new director with a clear vision. Ridley Scott made Alien, but Aliens was James Cameron's film, and it feels like it. Denis Villeneuve came to Blade Runner 2049 as a fan of the original and still made something that looks and moves in its own way. If you want to see this for yourself, watch an original and its sequel on consecutive nights and make a note of what each one is really about.

For readers, it is worth going back to the source material too. Frank Herbert's Dune Messiah reframes Paul's story in a way that makes Part Two's darker ending feel inevitable. The lesson from all of these films is simple. A sequel earns its place when it has something new to say, not just more to show. Next time a franchise announces another chapter, that is a good question to ask before you get excited.
ar-movies-animation: Every awards season, animated films get pushed into their own little category as if they're all the same kind of thing. They aren't. Animation is just a way of making a film.

Across the Spider-Verse mixes a dozen art styles in one movie to show how different each universe feels. Spirited Away builds a bathhouse full of spirits that live-action couldn't make feel as real. These are choices only animation lets you make.
If you still think of cartoons as kids' stuff, watch Perfect Blue, then Your Name, then Into the Spider-Verse, in that order.

Animation has been doing serious grown-up work for a long time. Grave of the Fireflies, directed by Isao Takahata for Studio Ghibli, is one of the most devastating war films ever made. Waltz with Bashir used animation to tell a documentary story about memory and war. Satoshi Kon, the director of Perfect Blue, went on to make Paprika, a dream-hopping thriller that people still compare to Inception. None of these would work in quite the same way if they had been shot with real actors and real sets.

Awards bodies have slowly caught up. Beauty and the Beast was nominated for Best Picture at the Oscars, and so were Up and Toy Story 3 years later. Spirited Away won Best Animated Feature, as did Miyazaki's The Boy and the Heron. More recently the Latvian film Flow, a story about a cat surviving a flood with no dialogue at all, won the same award. It's proof that you don't need a giant studio behind you to make something that matters.

If you want to widen your watchlist, try mixing techniques as well as countries. Aardman's Wallace and Gromit films show how much personality you can squeeze out of plasticine, and Laika's Coraline does the same for spooky stop-motion. Klaus, on Netflix, makes hand-drawn animation look like nothing you've seen before. Subtitles or dub is your call, and both are fine. The main thing is to judge each film on what it's trying to do, the same way you would with anything live-action.
ar-movies-theatre: Streaming is convenient, but some movies are designed for a giant screen and speakers that shake your seat. You lose a lot watching them on a laptop.

Directors who shoot on IMAX cameras frame their shots for that tall aspect ratio. The sound mix is built for a room full of speakers. A quiet moment in a packed theatre feels completely different from the same moment at home.
Then there's the crowd. Hearing a whole room gasp at a reveal is part of the experience, and it's something you only get once.

Christopher Nolan is probably the best-known champion of this. He shot large parts of Oppenheimer on IMAX 65mm film, including black-and-white IMAX footage, and the image fills the screen from floor to ceiling in the right venue. Denis Villeneuve's Dune films use an expanded aspect ratio in IMAX, so the desert and the sandworms get extra height you simply do not see at home. Top Gun: Maverick is another one people still talk about, with real jets and cockpit footage that feel far more intense on a huge screen.

If you want the full experience, it helps to know what you are booking. Not every IMAX screen is the same size, and only a handful of cinemas can show the full 1.43:1 ratio that some films are shot in. Dolby Atmos screens are great for sound even if the picture is standard. For seats, aim for the middle of the row and roughly two thirds of the way back, where the picture and sound are balanced. Many cinemas also offer student discounts, so bring your ID.

None of this means streaming is bad. Smaller dramas, comedies and dialogue-heavy films often work perfectly well on a sofa with the subtitles on. The point is to save your cinema money for the films that were built for it: the big spectacle, the loud action, the ones with a sound mix that has been talked about. When one of those comes out, try to catch it on the biggest screen you can reach before it disappears from cinemas.
ar-tv-finales: A bad finale can ruin a whole show on rewatch. A good one makes every season before it feel better.

Breaking Bad's last episode ties up Walter's story without feeling like a checklist. Fleabag ended after two short seasons with a scene at a bus stop that people still talk about. Arcane closed its story with a second season that went all in on its characters.
What these finales share is that the writers knew the ending early and built toward it. You can feel the difference when a show is making it up as it goes.

A few more deserve a mention. Six Feet Under ended with a closing montage that did exactly what the show had always been about, and it is still one of the most discussed finales in television. The Good Place wrapped up with an episode that took its big philosophical questions seriously and gave every main character a proper goodbye. Better Call Saul also managed a strong ending, which is impressive given how much it had to live up to.

Vince Gilligan famously pitched Breaking Bad as the story of a man going from Mr Chips to Scarface, and that clear idea is a big part of why the finale works. The destination was built into the premise. If you want to test this with your own favourite shows, try watching the pilot straight after the finale. The good ones feel like two halves of the same story, and you will often spot early scenes that were quietly pointing to the end.

It is also fair to say that a strong ending sometimes means a shorter show. Fleabag stopped at twelve episodes and Arcane at two seasons, and neither feels cut short. When you are choosing what to start next, a completed series with a well-loved finale can be more satisfying than something with no end in sight. Knowing a show lands its ending makes every episode on the way there feel like time well spent.
ar-tv-adaptations: For years, video game adaptations were a punchline. Then The Last of Us and Arcane came out close together and both became some of the best-reviewed shows of their years.

The difference is that both treated the source material as a story, not a brand. The Last of Us spent a whole episode on side characters who barely appear in the game. Arcane invented most of its plot and still felt like League of Legends.
The lesson for studios is simple: hire people who care about the characters, and don't just copy the cutscenes.

It helps to remember how bad things used to be. The 1993 Super Mario Bros. film and the 1994 Street Fighter movie are still brought up whenever someone wants an example of a studio missing the point. The Last of Us had the opposite approach. Craig Mazin, who made Chernobyl, worked alongside Neil Druckmann, who wrote the game, and the third episode about Bill and Frank earned Nick Offerman an Emmy. Arcane, animated by the French studio Fortiche, won the Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program.

Other shows have followed the same pattern. Fallout on Prime Video, from Jonathan Nolan and Lisa Joy, doesn't retell any of the games and instead tells a new story in the same world, which meant long-time players and complete newcomers could enjoy it together. Netflix's Castlevania took a series with very little plot and built a dark, character-driven story around it. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, made by Studio Trigger, did such a good job with Night City that lots of viewers went back to the game afterwards.

The good news for fans is that you don't need to have played anything to enjoy these shows, and you don't need to have watched the show to enjoy the games. Try one and see if it pulls you towards the other. If you already love the game, go in expecting changes rather than a copy, because some of the best moments in these adaptations are the ones nobody saw coming. That's usually a sign the people making it actually understood the story.
ar-tv-binge: Binge drops are great for a lazy weekend, but a lot of shows vanish from the conversation a week after release. Weekly episodes keep people talking for months.
When everyone watches at the same pace, you get theories, memes and those Monday morning conversations about who's lying. That shared waiting is half of what made old TV feel like an event.
Our take: mystery and thriller shows should go weekly. Comedies and comfort shows can drop all at once.

You can see the difference in how some of the biggest shows were released. Game of Thrones and Succession aired weekly on HBO, and each Sunday night turned into a small event online. Disney+ went weekly with The Mandalorian, and that helped Grogu become a meme long before the season ended. Apple TV+ released Severance weekly too, which gave fans a full week to argue about every hallway and every clue. Netflix has mostly stuck to binge drops, although it split Stranger Things 4 into two volumes to stretch the conversation out.

Whichever way a show arrives, there are ways to get more out of it. If it is a binge drop, try pacing yourself to an episode or two a night so the story has time to sink in. Watching with friends, in person or over a group chat, brings back some of that shared feeling. And if you know you will fall behind, mute the show's title and main characters' names on social media before the finale, because spoilers turn up everywhere within hours.

In the end, the release model matters less than whether the show is worth talking about. A great comedy still lands if you watch the whole thing in one sitting, and a weak thriller will not be saved by a weekly schedule. But when a mystery is genuinely good, being forced to wait turns it into something bigger than a show. You remember where you were for the twist, who you texted afterwards and which theory you got completely wrong.
ar-kpop-choreo: K-Pop choreography looks impossible the first time you try it. It isn't. It's just a lot of eight-counts in a row, and anyone can learn eight counts.
Start with mirrored dance practice videos, slow them to 0.75 speed and learn one chorus at a time. Record yourself early, because what feels right and what looks right are often different things.
Once you've got a song down, look for local dance cover groups. Random play dance events are the most fun you can have in a crowd of strangers who all know the same routine.

Not every routine is equally beginner friendly, so pick your first song carefully. Something with a famous point move, like the hand pose in TWICE's TT, is a good choice because the key moment is easy to learn and instantly recognisable. Save the dense, fast routines for later. Many groups' agencies post official dance practice videos on YouTube, which show the full choreography in plain clothes and a simple room, far easier to follow than a music video full of camera cuts.

Look after your body while you learn. Warm up properly before practising, wear trainers with some grip rather than socks on a slippery floor, and stretch afterwards. K-Pop routines use a lot of quick direction changes and floor work, and knees tend to complain first. Short, regular sessions of twenty or thirty minutes will get you further than one exhausting three-hour attempt, and you will remember the steps better when you come back to them.

The community side is where it really becomes fun. University societies and local cover groups often welcome beginners, and random play dance events are usually relaxed about people joining in only for the songs they know. Nobody expects you to be perfect, and most of the crowd will be cheering whoever is brave enough to step in. Learning choreography is less about talent than patience, and every dancer you admire started with a single eight-count.
ar-kpop-lightsticks: Early K-Pop fandoms showed up with coloured balloons in their group's official colour. Stadiums turned into seas of yellow, pink or pearl blue.

Lightsticks came next, and now each group has its own design that connects to the venue by Bluetooth, so the whole crowd changes colour in sync with the stage. At a big show it looks like a galaxy that knows the choreography.
For a lot of fans it's the first piece of merch they buy, and the one they keep long after the tour ends.

The balloon era is where a lot of fandom colours were set. Sechs Kies fans are known for yellow, Shinhwa for orange, and Super Junior's fandom for pearl sapphire blue, and older fans still take those colours seriously. When official lightsticks took over, BIGBANG's crown-shaped design became one of the most recognisable early examples. These days the designs are part of each group's identity, from BTS's ARMY Bomb to BLACKPINK's heart-topped hammer, which fans affectionately call the Hammer Bong, and TWICE's Candybong.

If you're buying your first one, go through the official store for the group's agency or an authorised seller. Fakes are common online, and even if they look right, they usually won't connect to the stadium system, which is the whole point. Before the concert, check whether the lightstick needs pairing through an app and whether you have to enter your seat details, because some models do. Bring spare batteries too. Nothing is sadder than a dark lightstick during the one song you were waiting for.

Plenty of fans also decorate theirs with stickers, charms and little photocards, and lightstick deco has become a small hobby of its own. Even without a concert coming up, many fans bring them out when watching livestreams or award shows at home. It's a simple bit of plastic and LEDs, but it tells everyone around you who you're there for, and when thousands of them light up in the same colour at once, it's easy to see why fans get so attached.
ar-kpop-global: Gangnam Style showed that a Korean song could go viral worldwide, but the real shift came from fandoms who organised online.

Fans subtitled variety shows overnight, ran streaming parties to push music videos up the charts and turned comeback days into global events. Agencies noticed and started releasing English content and touring in new markets.
Today K-Pop groups sell out stadiums in Lagos, London, São Paulo and Los Angeles, and a lot of that happened because fans refused to wait for the industry.

BTS are the clearest example of how far this went. The group played two nights at Wembley Stadium in 2019, and in 2020 Dynamite became the first song by a South Korean act to reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100. BLACKPINK headlined Coachella in 2023, which would have seemed unlikely a decade earlier. Behind all of these moments were fans who streamed, voted, bought albums and translated interviews, making sure each new release reached people who had never heard of the group before.

If you are new to the fandom, there is a lot of culture to pick up. Most groups have an official fandom name, an official lightstick for concerts and fan chants that crowds shout during specific songs. Platforms like Weverse let artists post updates and chat with fans directly. Supporting official releases, whether by streaming music videos or buying albums, matters far more than arguing online. And please respect idols' privacy: following them to airports or hotels is not being a fan, it is harassment.

It is also worth exploring beyond the biggest names. K-Pop has groups in almost every style, from polished pop to rock bands and hip hop crews, and many smaller acts have brilliant discographies that never trended worldwide. The fan communities that pushed K-Pop overseas were built by people sharing what they loved with anyone who would listen. That is still the best way to be part of it: find a song you like, pass it on and enjoy the ride.
ar-comics-start: The number one question new readers ask is where to start. The honest answer: anywhere with a number one on the cover and a creative team you like.
You don't need to know eighty years of history. Most runs are written to stand on their own. Batman: Year One, Miles Morales: Spider-Man and Ms. Marvel: No Normal are all good starting points.
Graphic novels and collected trade paperbacks are easier than tracking single issues. Your local library probably has more than you think.

If superheroes are not your thing, there is plenty more to choose from. Saga by Brian K. Vaughan and Fiona Staples is a space fantasy about a family on the run, and it is one of the most recommended series for new readers. Matt Fraction and David Aja's Hawkeye is a funny, stylish look at what an Avenger does on his days off. All-Star Superman by Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely tells a complete Superman story in twelve issues with no homework required.

A few practical tips help a lot. Reading apps like Marvel Unlimited and DC Universe Infinite let you try lots of series for one subscription, which is a cheap way to find out what you like. Many UK libraries also lend digital comics through apps such as Libby. Local comic shops are worth a visit too, because staff are usually happy to recommend something based on a film or show you already enjoy, and Free Comic Book Day each May is a good excuse to go.

Most importantly, follow creators rather than continuity. If you love how a particular writer or artist tells a story, look up what else they have worked on and you will often find your next favourite that way. Nobody has read everything, not even the people who work in comic shops. Pick something that looks interesting, read it and see where it takes you. That is really all there is to getting started.
ar-comics-multiverse: Comics started using parallel worlds as a way to keep old versions of characters around without breaking new stories. It got out of hand quickly.

DC has Crises that reset reality every so often. Marvel has numbered Earths, with the main one being Earth-616. The Spider-Verse films made the idea mainstream by showing how many different Spider-People could exist.
The easiest way to handle it is to not worry about it. Each story tells you which world it's set in, and that's all you need.

DC is where the idea really took off. In The Flash of Two Worlds, from 1961, Barry Allen's Flash meets Jay Garrick, the older Golden Age Flash, who lives on a separate Earth. That gave DC a way to bring back its classic heroes, and soon there were Earth-One, Earth-Two, Earth-Three and many more. By the mid-1980s it had become so tangled that Marv Wolfman and George Pérez wrote Crisis on Infinite Earths to clean it all up, and later crises kept doing the same job.

Marvel's version works slightly differently. Earth-616, a name popularised in Alan Moore's Captain Britain stories, is the main continuity, and alternate worlds are mostly places to visit. The Ultimate line, set on Earth-1610, is where Miles Morales first appeared as Spider-Man before he became the star of Into the Spider-Verse. Events like Secret Wars have smashed worlds together, and the Spider-Verse comic event brought Spider-People from all over the multiverse into one story long before the films did it on the big screen.

If you want to dip in, pick stories that are designed to stand on their own. Grant Morrison's The Multiversity is a tour of DC's many Earths that doesn't need years of homework, and the Spider-Verse comics are a fun follow-up to the films. Reading services like Marvel Unlimited and DC's own app make it easy to jump around. Don't feel you have to understand everything. Half the fun of the multiverse is meeting a strange new version of a character you already love.
ar-comics-indie: Superheroes dominate the shelves, but some of the best comics ever made have no capes in them.

Monstress is a dark fantasy with some of the most detailed art in the medium. Paper Girls is a time-travel adventure about four friends on a newspaper route. Persepolis and Maus prove that comics can tell true stories as powerfully as any book.
If you've only read superhero comics, try one of these. It might change what you think the medium is for.

There are plenty more where those came from. Saga, by Brian K. Vaughan and Fiona Staples, is a sprawling space opera about a family on the run, though it is very much for older readers. Bone by Jeff Smith is a funny, all-ages fantasy that many people read as kids and never forgot. Alison Bechdel's Fun Home is a moving memoir about her father, and Maus became the first graphic novel to receive a Pulitzer Prize, in the form of a special award in 1992.

You do not have to spend much to get started. Public libraries often have a solid graphic novel section, and many also lend digital comics through apps like Libby. Collected editions, usually called trade paperbacks, bundle several issues together and are the easiest way to read a whole story arc. If you have a local comic shop, the staff are usually happy to recommend something based on books or films you already like. Free Comic Book Day, held in many shops each May, is another easy way to try new series.

Comics that are not about superheroes also have a habit of reaching other screens. Paper Girls became a TV series, ND Stevenson's Nimona was turned into an animated film and Alice Oseman's Heartstopper found a huge audience on Netflix. Reading the original is often the best way to see what made them special in the first place. Whatever you pick, give it a few chapters, because the joy of indie comics is how different each one feels from the last.
ar-manga-weekly: Weekly manga moves fast, and so do spoilers. Chapters leak days early and the internet talks about them instantly.

Official apps now release many chapters in English on the same day as Japan, which is the best way to read and support the creators. Mute keywords for the series you follow the day before a new chapter drops.
And if you do get spoiled, remember that knowing what happens isn't the same as reading it. Great panels still hit.

The two main official options are Shueisha's MANGA Plus and the Shonen Jump app from VIZ Media, which between them carry series such as One Piece, Sakamoto Days and Kagurabachi alongside plenty of newer titles. Both let you read the latest chapters of many series for free, and paying for a subscription helps support the magazine. Reading on release day also means you are part of the conversation at the same time as everyone else, rather than playing catch-up with leaks.

Spoilers do not only come from text posts. Thumbnails on YouTube, fan art and trending tabs are where most people get caught out, so it is worth muting artist tags and series hashtags as well as character names. On Reddit, many series communities use spoiler tags and hold discussion threads until official release. Remember that weekly series take regular breaks too, so check a series' schedule before assuming a missing chapter means something has gone wrong.

Some fans skip the weekly chase entirely and wait for collected volumes, which come with cleaner art, author notes and often small corrections. There is no wrong way to read, as long as it works for you and supports the people who make it. If the weekly rhythm starts feeling more stressful than fun, try batching chapters once a month. The story will still be there, and it often reads better in bigger pieces anyway.
ar-manga-vs-anime: There's no single answer, but there are good rules of thumb.

If the anime has a strong studio behind it, like Jujutsu Kaisen or Frieren, watch the anime first and read the manga to continue the story. If the anime is known for filler or cut content, go straight to the manga. Black Clover and Solo Leveling, for example, go far beyond what the anime has covered so far.
Either way, the manga is where the story continues once you catch up with the show.

Some anime genuinely add something to the original. Mob Psycho 100, animated by Bones, turned ONE's rough, scratchy art into some of the most inventive fight scenes around, and the first season of One Punch Man did something similar with Madhouse. Frieren's gentle pacing and score make the quiet moments hit even harder. On the other hand, the second season of The Promised Neverland left out a huge chunk of the manga's story, so fans often point newcomers straight to the books once the first season ends.

There's a classic example of how much the order can matter. The first Fullmetal Alchemist anime caught up with the manga and went off in its own direction, while Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood came later and followed Hiromu Arakawa's story all the way to the end. Both have fans, but they're very different experiences. One small note on Solo Leveling, too: it's actually a Korean webtoon, or manhwa, rather than Japanese manga, and it reads top to bottom in full colour on your phone.

Whatever you pick, read legally where you can. Shueisha's Manga Plus and the Shonen Jump app carry lots of big series, often for free or very cheaply, and publishers like Viz, Yen Press and Kodansha sell collected volumes. When you want to carry on from the anime, look up which chapter the last episode covered, and start a few chapters earlier to catch any small scenes that were cut. Then you'll get the best of both without missing anything.
ar-manga-panels: Manga is read right to left, top to bottom. That includes the page order, the panels and the speech bubbles inside each panel.
It feels strange for about ten pages and then it becomes automatic. If you get lost, look for the panel in the top right corner and follow the flow from there.
Sound effects are usually left in Japanese with small translations next to them. After a while you start recognising them without the notes.

It helps to know why the direction is different. Japanese is traditionally written and read from right to left in books, so manga is printed that way too. Years ago some English editions were flipped to read left to right, but mirroring the art caused odd problems, like characters suddenly becoming left-handed. Most publishers now keep the original layout, and many English volumes even put a warning page at the back telling you that you have started from the wrong end.

A few more habits will make reading smoother. When two pages form one large image, called a spread, take it in as a single picture before moving on. If speech bubbles sit side by side, the one further right is usually read first, and bubbles higher on the page come before lower ones. Vertical comics like webtoons, often read on phones, work differently and simply scroll from top to bottom. Official apps such as Manga Plus and the Shonen Jump app are a legal and cheap way to practise with current series.

If you want an easy first series, pick something with clear, uncluttered pages. Spy x Family and Yotsuba&! are both popular choices for new readers because the layouts are easy to follow and the stories are fun from the first chapter. Once the flow clicks, busier action series like Chainsaw Man or Jujutsu Kaisen become much easier. Give yourself a volume or two, and you will soon be reading right to left without thinking about it at all.
nw-one-piece: One Piece has been running since 1999, and it is finally in its final saga. For new fans that number of episodes can feel scary, but the story is split into clear arcs, so it is easy to take in pieces.

The usual advice is to start at Romance Dawn and push through to Arlong Park. That is where most people get hooked. From there, Enies Lobby and Marineford are the two big emotional peaks everyone talks about.
If you are short on time, fan-made recap guides and the live-action series are both decent entry points. Once you know the crew, the anime picks up fast.

One Piece is the work of Eiichiro Oda, who launched the manga in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1997. It has gone on to sell more than 500 million copies worldwide, and Guinness World Records lists it as the most published comic series by a single author. The anime has been made by Toei Animation since 1999, and it has also produced a long run of films, including One Piece Film: Red in 2022, which became one of the biggest anime films of its year.

The final saga began in the manga in 2022, straight after the Wano Country arc. In the anime, the Egghead arc opened this last stretch, taking the crew to Dr. Vegapunk's island of science. Toei then took a short production break and brought the show back in April 2026 with the Elbaph arc, the land of the giants that fans have been waiting to see since Usopp first talked about it back in the early days.

One thing worth knowing is that the anime now runs on a new schedule of up to 26 episodes a year. Toei says this lets each episode cover more of the manga at a better pace, which should help with the slow feel some older arcs had. Netflix's live-action series is also still going, with Iñaki Godoy as Luffy, so there has never been an easier time to join the crew.
nw-demon-slayer: Demon Slayer's final arc takes place inside the Infinity Castle, a shifting fortress where the Hashira face the Upper Moons one by one. Instead of a TV season, it is being released as a trilogy of films.
Ufotable has always been known for its fire and water effects, and the castle gives them a whole new playground: rooms flip, floors turn into walls and every fight happens in a different space.
If you have not caught up, watch the Hashira Training season first. It sets up almost every duel in the castle.

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba started life as Koyoharu Gotouge's manga in Weekly Shonen Jump, and the anime has been made by ufotable since the first season aired in 2019. Haruo Sotozaki has directed the series throughout, and the music comes from Yuki Kajiura and Go Shiina. The main voice cast has stayed the same from the start, with Natsuki Hanae as Tanjiro, Akari Kito as Nezuko, Hiro Shimono as Zenitsu and Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Inosuke.

The first Infinity Castle film opened in Japan on 18 July 2025 and went on to become a record breaker. It passed Spirited Away to become the second highest-earning film ever at the Japanese box office, sitting only behind Demon Slayer's own Mugen Train, and it was the first Japanese film to earn more than 100 billion yen worldwide. It also won Best Animated Film at the Japan Academy Film Prizes.

The first film covers three of the big early clashes in the castle: Shinobu against Doma, Zenitsu against his former fellow student Kaigaku, and Tanjiro and Giyu against Akaza. That leaves plenty of the arc for the second and third films, including the fights against Kokushibo and, eventually, Muzan himself. If you missed it in cinemas, the first film is now on Crunchyroll with subtitles and several dubs.
nw-jujutsu-kaisen: The Culling Game is a battle royale spread across Japan, created by Kenjaku. Players are forced to fight, earn points and add new rules to the game.
Because the rules keep changing, this arc can be confusing on first watch. The short version: points come from defeating other players, and 100 points lets you add a rule.
Yuji, Megumi and their allies enter the game for different reasons, which splits the story into several parallel fights. It is chaotic, but that is the point.

Jujutsu Kaisen was created by Gege Akutami and ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2018 until the manga wrapped up in 2024. The anime is made by MAPPA, the studio also behind the final season of Attack on Titan, and it first aired in October 2020. In between the TV seasons came the Jujutsu Kaisen 0 film, which introduced Yuta Okkotsu, a character who matters a lot once the Culling Game gets going.

Season 3, officially titled The Culling Game Part 1, premiered in January 2026 with a one-hour special made up of its first two episodes. Director Shota Goshozono and series writer Hiroshi Seko both returned after their work on the Shibuya Incident season, and King Gnu came back to perform the opening theme, AIZO. The season finished with an extended 27-minute final episode, which gave the last fight of the part a bit more room to breathe.

The good news is that the story is not stopping there. MAPPA has confirmed Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4, The Culling Game Part 2, and showed a first teaser during its 15th anniversary livestream in June 2026. Takeru Sato, who was assistant director on Season 3, steps up to direct, while Hiroshi Seko stays on scripts. No release window has been given yet, so for now it is a good time to rewatch Part 1 and get the rules straight.
nw-naruto: Naruto follows a loud kid nobody believes in who decides to become the strongest ninja in his village. That underdog story is simple, and it works for almost everyone.
The show also has a lot of filler. Fans recommend using a filler guide so you do not get stuck in episodes that were made to let the manga get ahead.
The Chunin Exams arc is where most people fall in love with it, and the Pain arc in Shippuden is still one of the most talked-about fights in anime.

Naruto started life as a manga by Masashi Kishimoto, which ran in Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump from 1999 to 2014 and was collected into 72 volumes. It became one of the best-selling manga of all time, and it sat alongside One Piece and Bleach as one of the so-called Big Three that defined Shonen Jump for a whole generation of readers in the 2000s.

The anime was made by Studio Pierrot. The original series ran from 2002 to 2007 with 220 episodes, and Naruto Shippuden followed from 2007 to 2017 with another 500. Junko Takeuchi voices Naruto in Japanese and Maile Flanagan plays him in the English dub, and both versions have loyal fans. The music helps too: Blue Bird by Ikimonogakari is still one of the most loved anime openings around.

If you finish Shippuden and want more, the story carries on with Boruto, which follows Naruto's son. The sequel manga, Boruto: Two Blue Vortex, is written with Kishimoto back on board and is where the main story is heading now. There are also the Ultimate Ninja Storm games from CyberConnect2, which retell the big fights and are a fun way to relive the series.
nw-attack-on-titan: Attack on Titan ended with The Final Chapters, a two-part special that adapted the last volumes of the manga.
Few endings in anime have caused as much discussion. Some fans think Eren's path was set from the first episode, others feel the last chapters rushed the ending.
Whatever side you are on, the series is worth a rewatch. The first season hides a lot of clues that only make sense once you know the ending.

Attack on Titan began life as a manga by Hajime Isayama, serialised in Kodansha's Bessatsu Shonen Magazine from 2009 until April 2021. The finished story runs to 34 volumes, and Isayama added a few extra pages to the epilogue for the final collected volume, which is worth tracking down if you only read the chapters as they came out. It is still one of the best-selling manga of its era.

The anime changed hands partway through. Wit Studio made the first three seasons, starting in 2013, before MAPPA took over for The Final Season in December 2020. Hiroyuki Sawano's score and Linked Horizon's opening songs became part of the show's identity, and Yuki Kaji voiced Eren in Japanese throughout, with Bryce Papenbrook in the English dub. Both studios kept the look and tone surprisingly consistent.

The Final Chapters arrived as two long specials, the second airing in November 2023. Both parts were later edited together into a cinema release, Attack on Titan: The Last Attack, which gave fans a chance to see the ending on a big screen. With the story complete, the best thing to look forward to is sharing it with friends who have never seen it.
nw-my-hero-academia: My Hero Academia followed Izuku Midoriya from a Quirkless kid to the heir of One For All. The final season adapts the last war between the heroes and the League of Villains.
The show's biggest strength has always been its cast. Almost every student in Class 1-A gets a moment, and fans have favourites far beyond the main trio.
If you dropped the show during the middle seasons, the last arcs are a good reason to come back.

My Hero Academia was created by Kohei Horikoshi and ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from July 2014 to August 2024. The manga finished with 42 volumes, and the last one added extra pages that carry on after the ending, which gave fans a proper farewell to the class. Horikoshi's love of American superhero comics shows everywhere, from All Might's design to the way the hero agencies work like a real industry.

The anime has been made by Studio Bones since 2016, and the final season kept the same core team, including chief director Kenji Nagasaki, director Naomi Nakayama and composer Yuki Hayashi, whose music has been a big part of the show's best moments. The eighth season premiered in October 2025 and streamed on Crunchyroll. Daiki Yamashita voices Deku in Japanese, and Justin Briner leads the English dub.

Even with the main story finished, the world of My Hero Academia is not going anywhere. The spin-off My Hero Academia: Vigilantes got its own anime in 2025, following street-level heroes working without a licence a few years before Deku's time at U.A. There are also four films to catch up on, with You're Next in 2024 being the latest, so there is plenty left to watch after the finale.
nw-frieren: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End starts where most fantasy stories end: after the Demon King is defeated. The elf mage Frieren outlives her friends and sets out to understand them better.
The pace is gentle, but the fights are some of the best-animated in recent years. The First-Class Mage Exam arc in particular became a fan favourite.
It is a great pick if you want something emotional without being heavy all the time.

Frieren is written by Kanehito Yamada and drawn by Tsukasa Abe, and it has been running in Shogakukan's Weekly Shonen Sunday since 2020. It picked up the Manga Taisho Award and the New Creator Prize at the Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize in 2021, well before the anime arrived. The manga now has more than 30 million copies in circulation, although it is currently on hiatus so the creators can look after their health.

The anime is made by Madhouse. The first season ran from September 2023 to March 2024 under director Keiichiro Saito, with a soundtrack by Evan Call that fans still talk about. Atsumi Tanezaki voices Frieren, with Kana Ichinose as Fern and Chiaki Kobayashi as Stark. Soon after it started airing, the show climbed all the way to the top of MyAnimeList's user rankings.

Season 2 aired from January 2026, with Tomoya Kitagawa taking over as director, Mrs. Green Apple on the opening theme and milet on the ending. The good news is that a third season has already been confirmed for October 2027. It will adapt the Golden Land arc, which features Macht, one of the most interesting demons in the story, so there is a lot to look forward to.
nw-solo-leveling: Solo Leveling started as a Korean web novel and webtoon before its anime adaptation. The story follows Sung Jinwoo, who gains a system that lets him level up without limits.
The anime's second season covers the Shadow Monarch storyline, where Jinwoo's army of shadows really starts to grow.
It is a power fantasy through and through, and fans love it for exactly that.

Solo Leveling was written by Chugong, and the webtoon version was drawn by the artist DUBU of Redice Studio. DUBU sadly passed away in 2022, but his striking artwork is a big reason the webtoon became such a hit on digital platforms around the world. The story's mix of dungeon raids, game-style menus and a very quiet, very determined hero struck a chord with readers well before any anime was announced.

The anime is made by A-1 Pictures and directed by Shunsuke Nakashige, with music by Hiroyuki Sawano, who is known for his work on Attack on Titan. Season 1 aired in January 2024, and Season 2, subtitled Arise from the Shadow, followed in January 2025, streaming on Crunchyroll. K-Pop fans got a nice surprise too, as the Season 2 opening, ReawakeR, is performed by LiSA featuring Felix from Stray Kids.

If you have finished both seasons, there is still plenty left to adapt, as the anime has only covered part of the original story. Crunchyroll has said that more Solo Leveling is being worked on, though fans will need some patience before any new episodes arrive. In the meantime, the webtoon is complete, and there is also a mobile and PC game, Solo Leveling: Arise, from Netmarble.
nw-gta-6: GTA VI is set in the fictional state of Leonida, based on Florida, with Vice City as its main city. The story follows Lucia and Jason, a criminal couple.
The first trailer broke YouTube viewing records within a day. The game is coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC date announced yet.
Release dates have moved before, so keep an eye on Rockstar's official channels before planning a launch night.

Grand Theft Auto VI is being made by Rockstar Games, with Rockstar North in Edinburgh leading development as it has on the main series for years. It is the first new main entry since Grand Theft Auto V in 2013, which went on to sell more than 200 million copies. That long gap is a big part of why the wait has felt so intense.

The first trailer arrived in December 2023 and set the tone: sunny beaches, neon nightlife and a social media twist on Florida news stories. A second trailer followed in May 2025, giving fans a much closer look at Jason and Lucia and at the wider state of Leonida, including swamps, small towns and the busy streets of Vice City. It was the clearest look yet at how the two leads work together.

Rockstar has delayed the game twice. It is now set to launch on 19 November 2026, a date Rockstar confirmed on its official Newswire, where the studio apologised for the extra wait and said the time would let it finish the game to the level of polish players expect. Pre-launch details such as editions and extra trailers are worth watching for on Rockstar's own channels.
nw-zelda-totk: Tears of the Kingdom added sky islands and a huge underground Depths to the Hyrule from Breath of the Wild.
Its biggest feature is Ultrahand, which lets you glue objects together. Players have built planes, tanks and even working machines that walk.
If you liked Breath of the Wild but want more creativity, this is the one.

Tears of the Kingdom launched on Nintendo Switch in May 2023. It was made by Nintendo's EPD team, with Hidemaro Fujibayashi directing and long-time series producer Eiji Aonuma overseeing it, the same pairing behind Breath of the Wild. Nintendo said it sold over ten million copies in its first three days. Both games share a version of Hyrule, but the sequel changes a lot of it, with new caves, towns and characters to meet along the way.

Ultrahand is only part of Link's new toolkit. Fuse lets you stick items onto weapons, shields and arrows, Ascend lets you swim up through ceilings, and Recall rewinds an object's movement. Autobuild, found later, lets you save a favourite creation and rebuild it in seconds, which is why so many player machines now get shared and copied online. It is a big step up from the physics tricks in Breath of the Wild.

The game won Best Action/Adventure Game at The Game Awards in 2023, and a Nintendo Switch 2 Edition later added a sharper picture and smoother frame rate. Looking ahead, fans have Nintendo and Sony's live-action Legend of Zelda film, directed by Wes Ball, to look forward to, with Bo Bragg as Zelda and Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link. It is a good time to be a Zelda fan.
nw-elden-ring: Elden Ring is FromSoftware's biggest open world. Unlike earlier Souls games, you can ride away from a boss that is too hard and come back later.
Spirit ashes and summons are there to help. Using them is part of the design, not cheating.
The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion adds a whole new region, but it is meant for players who have finished most of the base game.

Elden Ring came out in February 2022 and was directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, the creator of Dark Souls. Bandai Namco published it, and fantasy author George R. R. Martin helped write the world's backstory and mythology. It won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2022 and is now seen as one of the best open-world games ever made, even by players who had never touched a Souls game before.

A few habits make the early game much kinder. Explore Limgrave before charging into Stormveil Castle, because Margit and Godrick are tough for a new character. Rest at every Site of Grace you find, since they act as checkpoints and fast travel points. Keep an eye out for catacombs and caves too, as they often hold spirit ashes, upgrade materials and useful talismans that make the main bosses easier.

Shadow of the Erdtree came out in June 2024 and takes you to the Land of Shadow. To get in, you need to beat Starscourge Radahn and Mohg, Lord of Blood, which is why it is best left until late in a playthrough. It also has its own levelling system using Scadutree Fragments, so everyone starts on the back foot. GameSpot gave it a perfect ten, calling it every bit as good as the main game.
nw-god-of-war: Ragnarök continues the Norse saga that started in God of War (2018). Atreus is older and wants answers, and Kratos has to decide how much to protect him.
The combat is heavier and faster than before, with the Leviathan Axe and the Blades of Chaos both returning.
The free Valhalla add-on turns the game into a roguelike and gives Kratos one of his best moments.

Ragnarök was made by Santa Monica Studio and released for PS4 and PS5 in November 2022, with a PC version following in 2024. Eric Williams directed it, taking over from Cory Barlog, who led the 2018 game. Christopher Judge returns as Kratos and Sunny Suljic as Atreus, and Bear McCreary is back on the score, which is full of the Norse choirs and drums that made the first game sound so big.

The game did very well at The Game Awards 2022, winning several categories including Best Performance for Christopher Judge and Innovation in Accessibility. That last one matters, as Ragnarök has a huge list of options for controls, visuals and difficulty, so a lot more players can reach the end. It also brings in fan favourites from Norse myth, such as Thor, Odin and Freya, each with their own side of the story.

Valhalla arrived in December 2023 as a free download for anyone who owns the game. It works as an epilogue, with Kratos facing trials that make him look back at his past in Greece. Each run resets your stats and perks, so you have to adapt every time, but you keep some upgrades between attempts. Santa Monica recommends finishing the main story first to avoid spoilers.
nw-witcher-3: The Witcher 3 follows Geralt as he searches for Ciri. Its side quests are famous for being as well written as the main story.
The next-gen update added better graphics and quality-of-life changes, and the two expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, are often called better than most full games.
With a new Witcher game in development, now is a good time to catch up.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was developed by CD Projekt Red, the Polish studio later known for Cyberpunk 2077, and released in May 2015. It is based on the fantasy books by Andrzej Sapkowski, though the games tell their own story after the novels end. In English, Geralt is voiced by Doug Cockle, whose gravelly delivery has become a big part of the character for many players. The game won Game of the Year at The Game Awards in 2015.

Its sales have kept climbing long after launch. In May 2026, CD Projekt said the game had passed 65 million copies sold worldwide, putting it among the best-selling video games ever made. That is an impressive number for a single-player RPG, and it shows how word of mouth, regular sales and the next-gen update have kept bringing in new players year after year.

There is more on the way for Geralt, too. CD Projekt Red has announced a new expansion called Songs of the Past, planned for 2027 and co-developed with Fool's Theory. After that, the series moves on to The Witcher 4, which puts Ciri in the lead role as a witcher in her own right. It was first revealed with a trailer at The Game Awards in December 2024.
nw-halo-infinite: Halo Infinite takes place on Zeta Halo, a damaged ring world that you can explore in any order once the campaign opens up.
The grappleshot changed how players move and fight, and it is the tool people miss most when they go back to older Halo games.
Multiplayer is free to play and still gets regular updates.

Halo Infinite was developed by 343 Industries and published by Xbox Game Studios. The multiplayer launched early on 15 November 2021 to mark twenty years of Halo, and the campaign followed on 8 December 2021 for Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S and PC. It came after a one-year delay, when the team took extra time following a mixed reaction to its first gameplay reveal.

The campaign mixes open areas with more traditional Halo missions. You can wander Zeta Halo, retake outposts, rescue marines and hunt down targets, then head into linear story levels for the big moments. Reviews were warm, and GameSpot gave the campaign a 9 out of 10, singling out the grappleshot as the standout addition to Master Chief's toolkit. Many reviewers also praised the Chief's new AI companion, known as the Weapon.

343 Industries has since been renamed Halo Studios, and the team has moved on to new projects built in Unreal Engine 5. Operation: Infinite, released in November 2025, was announced as the last major planned content update, though the studio said challenges, ranked seasons and events would continue. Its next release, Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the original game's campaign, launched in July 2026.
nw-call-of-duty: Call of Duty is split into sub-series: Modern Warfare, Black Ops and others. Each has its own campaign story.
For multiplayer, the newest release has the most players. Warzone, the free battle royale, is the easiest way to try the series without buying anything.
Zombies mode, mostly found in Black Ops games, is a co-op favourite with its own long-running story.

The series started in 2003 with a Second World War shooter from Infinity Ward, published by Activision. Things changed with Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare in 2007, which moved the action to the present day and set the template for the online multiplayer most fans know. Microsoft now owns the series after buying Activision Blizzard in 2023. Since then a new main game has arrived almost every autumn.

Several studios share the work. Infinity Ward leads the Modern Warfare games, Treyarch makes Black Ops, and Sledgehammer Games has handled entries such as Vanguard. Treyarch also created Zombies, which first appeared as a hidden bonus mode in World at War in 2008 before growing into a mode of its own. Warzone followed as a free battle royale in March 2020.

If you want a story to start with, the 2019 Modern Warfare reboot is a clean entry point that does not expect you to know the older games. Black Ops fans can follow the thread through to Black Ops 7, released in November 2025 and set in 2035, with a campaign built for co-op play and Menendez back as the villain.
nw-roblox: Everything on Roblox is made by its community using Roblox Studio. Some of the most popular experiences were made by teenagers.
Popular genres include obbies (obstacle courses), tycoons, role-play towns and horror games.
Parents can set age and spending controls from the account settings.

Roblox was founded by David Baszucki and Erik Cassel and launched to the public in 2006. It is free to play on PC, Mac, phones, tablets, Xbox and PlayStation, and it uses its own currency called Robux. Players spend Robux on avatar items and in-game extras, and that money is how creators get paid for the games they build, which is a big reason so many people take making things on Roblox seriously.

Roblox Studio is free to download, and games are scripted in Luau, a language based on Lua that is known for being friendly to beginners. Through the Developer Exchange programme, creators can swap the Robux they earn for real money. According to Roblox, creators earned more than 1.5 billion US dollars on the platform in 2025, and most of the creators it surveyed work on their own rather than as part of a big studio.

Some experiences have become huge names in their own right. Adopt Me!, Brookhaven, Blox Fruits and Grow a Garden have all pulled in massive numbers of players, and trends can change very quickly, with a small project turning into the biggest thing on the platform in weeks. For parents, Roblox also lets a parent link their own account to a child's to manage screen time and chat.
nw-genshin-impact: Genshin Impact's world is split into seven nations, each based on a different element and culture: Mondstadt (Anemo), Liyue (Geo), Inazuma (Electro), Sumeru (Dendro), Fontaine (Hydro), Natlan (Pyro) and Snezhnaya (Cryo).
Each nation brings a new story chapter, new characters and a new archon to meet.
The game is free to play, and the story can be completed without spending money.

Genshin Impact is developed by miHoYo and published under its HoYoverse brand. It launched in September 2020 on PC, PlayStation 4, iOS and Android, and has since reached PS5 and Xbox as well. You play as the Traveler, who arrives in Teyvat looking for a lost twin, with the small floating companion Paimon along for the ride. The game won Best Mobile Game at The Game Awards 2021.

Each nation is ruled by an archon, a god tied to one element. Mondstadt was the first region at launch, and every new nation since has arrived in a big yearly update. Natlan, the sixth nation, came with Version 5.0 in August 2024. It is built around tribes, dragons and a festival of combat, and it introduced Mavuika, the Pyro Archon, along with new ways to travel such as surfing on lava and water.

That leaves Snezhnaya, the cold northern nation that is home to the Cryo Archon, known as the Tsaritsa, and her Fatui agents. The Fatui have been causing trouble since the very first chapter, so fans have been expecting it to be the story's final stop for a long time. Until then, there are plenty of world quests, events and older regions to catch up on.
nw-minecraft: Minecraft lets you build anything from blocks. Survival mode adds hunger, monsters and resources, while Creative mode gives you everything for free.
Recent updates have added new biomes, mobs and trial chambers to explore.
It is also used in schools to teach coding, maths and teamwork.

Minecraft was created by Markus Persson, better known as Notch, and first appeared as an early build in 2009 before its full release in November 2011. It was developed by his studio Mojang, which Microsoft bought in 2014 for 2.5 billion US dollars. Today the game comes in two main versions, Java Edition on PC and Bedrock Edition, which lets players on consoles, phones and PCs play together.

In October 2023, during Minecraft Live, Mojang announced that the game had become the first single video game to sell more than 300 million copies. At the time, its closest rival, Grand Theft Auto V, was well behind. A huge part of that success comes from the community, from YouTube creators and speedrunners to the people who build entire cities and working computers out of blocks.

Minecraft has also moved beyond games. A Minecraft Movie, directed by Jared Hess and starring Jack Black as Steve alongside Jason Momoa, reached cinemas in 2025 and was a major box office success. On the game side, Mojang now releases smaller updates more often through the year and shares plans at its regular Minecraft Live shows, so there is usually something new to explore.
nw-dune-2: Dune: Part Two follows Paul as he joins the Fremen and rises as a leader. It was praised for its huge desert scenes and sound design.
The next film adapts Dune Messiah, the second book, which shows the darker side of Paul's rise.
If you have not read the books, the films work on their own, but the novels go much deeper into the politics.

Both films are based on Frank Herbert's 1965 novel Dune, which Denis Villeneuve split across two films. Part Two came out in March 2024 with Timothée Chalamet as Paul and Zendaya as Chani, joined by Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem and Josh Brolin, plus new faces Austin Butler as Feyd-Rautha and Florence Pugh as Princess Irulan. Hans Zimmer returned for the score.

The film made more than 700 million dollars worldwide and was nominated for Best Picture at the Academy Awards. It won two Oscars, for Best Sound and Best Visual Effects, following the six won by the first film. Plenty of fans and critics now put it alongside the best science fiction films of recent years, and the sandworm riding scene in particular is often picked out as a highlight.

Dune: Part Three is due in cinemas on 18 December 2026. Chalamet, Zendaya, Ferguson, Bardem and Pugh are all back, Jason Momoa returns as Hayt, Anya Taylor-Joy plays Paul's sister Alia and Robert Pattinson joins as the villain Scytale. Villeneuve has said he wants this chapter to feel different with its own identity, and parts of it were shot with IMAX cameras.
nw-spider-verse: Across the Spider-Verse mixes dozens of animation styles. Gwen's world looks like a watercolour painting, while Mumbattan is inspired by Indian comics.
The team wanted each Spider-Person to feel like they came from a different comic book.
The story ends on a cliffhanger that leads directly into Beyond the Spider-Verse.

Across the Spider-Verse came out in June 2023 as the sequel to Into the Spider-Verse, which won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. It was directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K. Thompson, written by Phil Lord, Christopher Miller and David Callaham, and animated by Sony Pictures Imageworks for Sony Pictures Animation. The film builds directly on the techniques the first one pioneered, blending computer animation with hand-drawn detail.

The voice cast helps sell each world. Shameik Moore returns as Miles and Hailee Steinfeld as Gwen, while Oscar Isaac plays Miguel O'Hara, Daniel Kaluuya plays Hobie the Spider-Punk, Karan Soni plays Pavitr Prabhakar and Jason Schwartzman plays The Spot. Hobie's look borrows from punk posters and cut-up collage, and he is often animated at a different frame rate to everyone around him.

Miguel's Nueva York was inspired by the futurist designs of Syd Mead, which is why it feels so clean and bright next to Gwen's painted Earth-65. The film swept the Annie Awards, including Best Feature, and was nominated for an Oscar. The story continues in Beyond the Spider-Verse, which Sony Pictures Animation is making now. Expect Miles to face the fallout of the cliffhanger head on.
nw-avengers-doomsday: Avengers: Doomsday brings together heroes from across the Marvel universe, with Robert Downey Jr. returning to the MCU as Doctor Doom.
The film is directed by the Russo brothers, who also made Infinity War and Endgame.
Release dates can change, so check Marvel's official channels for the latest schedule.

Downey's casting was revealed at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2024, where he took off a Doom mask on stage in Hall H. It was a big moment, since he spent more than a decade as Tony Stark before Iron Man's farewell in Endgame. Doctor Doom himself first appeared in Fantastic Four #5 in 1962, created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, and he has long been seen as one of Marvel's greatest villains.

The cast is one of the biggest Marvel has ever put together. Marvel's official page lists names such as Chris Hemsworth, Anthony Mackie, Florence Pugh, Paul Rudd, Sebastian Stan and Tom Hiddleston, alongside Pedro Pascal and Vanessa Kirby from The Fantastic Four: First Steps. Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen are back from the original X-Men films, and Chris Evans is listed too, which has fans guessing about how everyone fits together.

Marvel currently lists the release date as 18 December 2026. The script is by Stephen McFeely, who co-wrote Infinity War and Endgame, and Michael Waldron, head writer on Loki. Doomsday is also the first half of a two-part finale for this era of the MCU, with Avengers: Secret Wars following in 2027, so it is worth catching up on the multiverse stories before it arrives.
nw-endgame: Endgame picks up after Thanos wipes out half of all life. The remaining Avengers try one last plan to bring everyone back.
The final battle, with every hero returning through portals, is still one of the loudest cinema moments fans remember.
It also closed the stories of Iron Man and Captain America, which made it feel like the end of an era.

Endgame was directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, who also made Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Civil War and Infinity War. The script is by Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely, and it follows straight on from the ending of Infinity War. The cast is huge, led by Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Scarlett Johansson, Mark Ruffalo, Chris Hemsworth and Jeremy Renner, with Josh Brolin returning as Thanos.

The film was released in April 2019 and set a new record for a worldwide opening weekend. In July 2019 it passed Avatar to become the highest-grossing film of all time, earning around 2.79 billion dollars. Avatar later took the top spot back after a re-release in China, which leaves Endgame in second place on the all-time list, a remarkable result for a film that depends on over twenty earlier ones.

The Russo brothers are returning to the Avengers for Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars. The big twist in the announcement was that Robert Downey Jr. is back, this time playing Doctor Doom instead of Tony Stark. It is a good excuse to rewatch Endgame and look again at how it wrapped up the first era of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
nw-interstellar: Interstellar follows a team travelling through a wormhole to find humanity a new home.
The black hole Gargantua was created using real physics equations, and the research even led to scientific papers.
The film's emotional core, a father and daughter separated by time, is what keeps people coming back to it.

Interstellar was released in 2014, directed by Christopher Nolan and co-written with his brother Jonathan Nolan. Matthew McConaughey plays Cooper, a former pilot turned farmer, with Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Mackenzie Foy and Michael Caine in key roles. Kip Thorne, the physicist who helped shape the project from its early days, also served as an executive producer and wrote a companion book, The Science of Interstellar.

The black hole was built by the London visual effects company Double Negative, now DNEG. Its team wrote new rendering software that followed how light bends around a spinning black hole, working from equations supplied by Thorne. The results were published in the journal Classical and Quantum Gravity in 2015, and the film won the Oscar for Best Visual Effects. Thorne went on to share the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics for gravitational wave research.

The music matters just as much. Hans Zimmer's score leans heavily on a church organ, recorded at the Temple Church in London, which gives the film its huge, almost religious sound. Interstellar is also one of Nolan's most rewatched films, and it returned to IMAX cinemas for its tenth anniversary in 2024. If you have only seen it on a small screen, a big screen showing is worth catching.
nw-matrix: The Matrix follows Neo, a hacker who learns the world is a simulation built by machines.
Its bullet-time effect, where the camera moves around frozen action, was copied in films, games and adverts for years.
The sequels and the 2021 Resurrections film continue the story, though fans still argue over which is best.

The Matrix was written and directed by the Wachowskis and released in 1999. Keanu Reeves played Neo, with Laurence Fishburne as Morpheus, Carrie-Anne Moss as Trinity and Hugo Weaving as Agent Smith. It was shot in Sydney, Australia, and the fight scenes were choreographed by Hong Kong legend Yuen Woo-ping, which is a big reason the martial arts look so sharp.

It was a huge hit, taking more than 460 million dollars worldwide, and it won all four Academy Awards it was nominated for, including Best Visual Effects and Best Film Editing. It also sold brilliantly on DVD, helping the format take off. In 2012 it was added to the US National Film Registry for its cultural importance, a rare honour for a film that was only thirteen years old at the time.

The story grew well beyond the first film. The Matrix Reloaded and The Matrix Revolutions both came out in 2003, alongside The Animatrix, an anthology of animated shorts, and the game Enter the Matrix. Resurrections was directed by Lana Wachowski on her own. Warner Bros has since announced a fifth film, written and directed by Drew Goddard, with Lana Wachowski as executive producer.
nw-stranger-things: Stranger Things started in 2016 with a missing boy and a girl with psychic powers. It ended with a final season built around Vecna and the Upside Down.
The show made 80s music, arcades and Dungeons & Dragons popular with a new generation.
A spin-off animated series and a stage play continue the universe.

The show was created by Matt and Ross Duffer, known as the Duffer Brothers, and premiered on Netflix in July 2016. Shawn Levy joined as an executive producer and directed several episodes. The young cast, including Millie Bobby Brown, Finn Wolfhard, Gaten Matarazzo, Caleb McLaughlin and Noah Schnapp, grew up on screen alongside Winona Ryder and David Harbour. Natalia Dyer, Charlie Heaton, Joe Keery and Sadie Sink also became fan favourites as the story went on.

The final season was released in three parts. Volume 1 arrived on 26 November 2025, Volume 2 on Christmas Day, and the finale on New Year's Eve, when it was also shown in selected cinemas.
