That made the last episode feel like an event, with fans gathering to watch the ending together rather than on their own at home. It is a lovely way to end a show that fans have followed for almost a decade.

The show's influence on music was hard to miss. Season 4 sent Kate Bush's Running Up That Hill back up the charts in 2022, reaching number one in the UK decades after its first release. The stage prequel, Stranger Things: The First Shadow, opened in London's West End in 2023 before moving to Broadway. It tells the story of Henry Creel as a teenager in 1959.
nw-arcane: Arcane tells the story of sisters Vi and Jinx in the cities of Piltover and Zaun, from the world of League of Legends.
Its painterly animation style took years to develop, and it won several major animation awards.
Season 2 finished the story, so it can be watched in full.

Arcane was created by Christian Linke and Alex Yee at Riot Games and animated by Fortiche, a studio based in Paris. The first season premiered on Netflix in November 2021. Hailee Steinfeld voices Vi and Ella Purnell voices Jinx, with Katie Leung as Caitlyn and Reed Shannon as Ekko. The show also leans heavily on music, and Imagine Dragons' Enemy became its theme song and a hit in its own right.

The awards came quickly. In 2022 Arcane won the Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program, the first streaming series to take that prize, and it swept the Annie Awards the same year, including the top award for a TV or media production. Critics praised how it felt like a hand-painted piece of art in motion, and plenty of viewers who had never played League of Legends ended up hooked on it.

Season 2 arrived in November 2024 in three acts, and it is the final season of the story. Linke has said it is only the beginning of Riot's larger storytelling plans for Runeterra, the world where League of Legends is set, so this is unlikely to be the last we see of it on screen. For now, both seasons are on Netflix, making it a perfect series to binge from start to finish.
nw-last-of-us: The Last of Us follows Joel and Ellie across a United States ruined by a fungal outbreak.
The series takes time with side stories, like the much-praised third episode about Bill and Frank.
Season 2 adapts the start of The Last of Us Part II, and more seasons are planned to finish the story.

The series was created for HBO by Craig Mazin, the writer behind Chernobyl, and Neil Druckmann, who wrote and directed the original Naughty Dog game. It premiered in January 2023 with Pedro Pascal as Joel and Bella Ramsey as Ellie. Gustavo Santaolalla, who scored the games, also wrote music for the show, so a lot of it sounds just like fans remember.

Season 1 earned 24 Primetime Emmy nominations and is one of the highest-rated drama series in HBO's history. The Bill and Frank episode, Long, Long Time, starred Nick Offerman and Murray Bartlett, and Offerman went on to win the Emmy for guest actor. Season 2 arrived in April 2025, adding Kaitlyn Dever as Abby, Isabela Merced as Dina and Jeffrey Wright as Isaac.

HBO renewed the show for a third season before Season 2 had even aired. Mazin has said the adaptation of The Last of Us Part II needs one or two more seasons to finish, so Season 3 will keep working through the second game's story. Druckmann has since stepped back from the show to focus on Naughty Dog's games, leaving Mazin to lead it.
nw-wednesday: Wednesday follows the Addams family's daughter as she solves murders at a school for outcasts.
Jenna Ortega's dance scene in Season 1 became one of the biggest viral moments of its year.
Season 2 brings more of the Addams family into the story.

Wednesday was created by Alfred Gough and Miles Millar, the pair behind Smallville, and Tim Burton directs episodes and executive produces. The first season arrived on Netflix in November 2022 and became one of the platform's most-watched English-language series. Jenna Ortega leads the cast, with Catherine Zeta-Jones and Luis Guzman as Morticia and Gomez, and Emma Myers as Enid, Wednesday's cheerful werewolf roommate.

Season 2 was released in two parts, with Part 2 landing on Netflix on 3 September 2025. Pugsley enrols at Nevermore, which means Wednesday's family and school life collide much more than before. New faces include Steve Buscemi as the new principal, Barry Dort, Joanna Lumley as Grandmama, and Lady Gaga as Rosaline Rotwood, a legendary Nevermore teacher. Ortega also stepped up as an executive producer this time.

The show has already been renewed for a third season, and Netflix has confirmed that it is in production, with Lena Headey and Eva Green among the new cast members. The series also moved its filming from Romania to Ireland for Season 2, which gave Nevermore a slightly different, very gothic look. Until Season 3 arrives, it is a perfect time to go back and spot the clues you missed first time.
nw-breaking-bad: Breaking Bad follows a chemistry teacher who starts making meth after a cancer diagnosis.
The show is famous for planting small details that pay off seasons later.
Better Call Saul and the film El Camino continue the universe.

Breaking Bad was created by Vince Gilligan, who had previously written for The X-Files. It premiered on AMC in January 2008 and ran for five seasons and 62 episodes, finishing in 2013. It was filmed and set in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and the desert landscapes became as much a part of the show's look as its characters. Gilligan famously pitched the idea as turning Mr Chips into Scarface.

Bryan Cranston won four Emmys for playing Walter White, and Aaron Paul won three as Jesse Pinkman. The show also won Outstanding Drama Series in 2013 and 2014. Its ratings grew hugely over its run as people caught up on streaming, and the episode Ozymandias is still regularly named one of the best hours of television ever made. Giancarlo Esposito's Gus Fring also became one of TV's most famous villains.

Better Call Saul ran from 2015 to 2022, with Bob Odenkirk as Jimmy McGill, and many fans now rate it just as highly. El Camino, released on Netflix in 2019, follows Jesse after the finale. Gilligan has since moved on to something new with Pluribus, an Apple TV series starring Rhea Seehorn, who played Kim Wexler in Better Call Saul.
nw-game-of-thrones: Game of Thrones followed noble families fighting for the Iron Throne while the White Walkers threatened the North.
House of the Dragon, set two centuries earlier, tells the story of the Targaryen civil war.
More spin-offs set in Westeros are in development.

Game of Thrones ran on HBO from 2011 to 2019 across eight seasons and 73 episodes. David Benioff and D. B. Weiss adapted it from George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire novels, the first of which was published in 1996. Fans are still waiting for the sixth book, The Winds of Winter, so the show's ending remains the only finished version of the story.

The series won Outstanding Drama Series at the Emmys four times, and Peter Dinklage won four Emmys for playing Tyrion Lannister. It also made stars of Emilia Clarke, Kit Harington, Sophie Turner and Maisie Williams. House of the Dragon, run by Ryan Condal and based on Martin's history book Fire & Blood, has been planned as a four-season story. Its third season aired in 2026.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms is the newest addition. It premiered on HBO in January 2026 and adapts The Hedge Knight, the first of Martin's Dunk and Egg novellas. Peter Claffey plays Ser Duncan the Tall and Dexter Sol Ansell plays his squire Egg. Set about a century before Game of Thrones, it is a smaller, warmer story than the main series.
nw-bts: BTS debuted in 2013 and became one of the biggest music acts in the world with songs like Dynamite, Butter and Spring Day.
All members completed their mandatory military service, and fans have been celebrating the group's return to full activities.
The members also have solo albums that show their own styles.

BTS debuted under Big Hit Entertainment, now BIGHIT MUSIC, on 13 June 2013. The seven members are RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jungkook. Their early albums dealt with school life and growing up, and the Love Yourself series took them to a worldwide audience. Dynamite became their first number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2020, and it also earned them their first Grammy nomination.

Jin was the first to enlist, in December 2022, and Suga was the last to finish, completing his service in June 2025. Soon after, all seven held a Weverse live stream to say they would be working on music together again. They confirmed plans for their first full group album in four years and a world tour, both set for spring 2026, which was the news ARMY had been waiting for.

While the group was on break, the solo work kept fans busy. Jimin's Like Crazy and Jungkook's Seven both reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100. RM released Indigo, J-Hope put out Jack in the Box, Suga has released music as Agust D, V brought out Layover and Jin released Happy. If you are new, the solo albums are also a great way to find a favourite member.
nw-blackpink: BLACKPINK debuted in 2016 and became one of the most-streamed girl groups in the world. Their fandom is called BLINK.
All four members, Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé and Lisa, have released solo music and appear in film, fashion and TV.
The group continues to come together for world tours and group releases.

BLACKPINK were formed by YG Entertainment and debuted in August 2016 with the single album Square One, which included Whistle and Boombayah. Hits such as DDU-DU DDU-DU, Kill This Love and How You Like That followed. Their album Born Pink topped the Billboard 200 in 2022, making them the first K-Pop girl group to do so, and in 2023 they became the first Asian act to headline Coachella.

Each member has built a strong solo career. Rosé had a worldwide hit with APT., her duet with Bruno Mars, and followed it with her album rosie. Jennie released her first full album, Ruby, in 2025. Lisa released Alter Ego and made her acting debut in the third season of HBO's The White Lotus, while Jisoo has released solo music and also works as an actress in Korean dramas.

The group came back together in July 2025 for the DEADLINE world tour, which opened with two nights at Goyang Stadium in South Korea. More than 78,000 fans attended, and the group performed a new song, JUMP, for the first time there. The tour then moved on to cities across the world, with each member also getting a solo stage in the set.
nw-stray-kids: Stray Kids are an eight-member group under JYP Entertainment. Their producing unit, 3RACHA, is made up of Bang Chan, Changbin and Han.
Their style is loud and experimental, and they call it noise music.
They have topped the US Billboard 200 several times.

Stray Kids were formed through a 2017 survival show of the same name and debuted in March 2018. The line-up is Bang Chan, Lee Know, Changbin, Hyunjin, Han, Felix, Seungmin and I.N, and Bang Chan is the group's leader. Their fans are called STAY. Songs like District 9, God's Menu, Thunderous and Maniac helped build their reputation for bold, heavy tracks with big choruses and very sharp choreography.

Their US chart record is remarkable. ODDINARY became their first Billboard 200 number one in 2022, and every album since has debuted in the same spot. In August 2026, THIS & THAT gave them a ninth number one, making them the first act in the chart's 70-year history whose first nine entries all debuted at the top. That also tied them with The Rolling Stones for the second-most number one albums by a group.

The members also pop up in some fun places. Felix sings on ReawakeR, the Season 2 opening of the Solo Leveling anime, alongside LiSA, and the group's 2024 single Chk Chk Boom had a music video featuring Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman. With their record still unbroken, fans will be watching closely to see whether their next release can take them into double figures.
nw-twice: TWICE was formed through the survival show SIXTEEN and debuted with Like OOH-AHH.
Songs like Cheer Up, TT and Fancy made them one of the biggest girl groups in Korea and Japan.
The sub-unit MISAMO, made up of the three Japanese members, has also released its own music.

TWICE are a nine-member group under JYP Entertainment: Nayeon, Jeongyeon, Momo, Sana, Jihyo, Mina, Dahyun, Chaeyoung and Tzuyu, with Jihyo as leader. They debuted in October 2015, and their mix of members from Korea, Japan and Taiwan helped them build a big following across Asia early on. Their fandom is called ONCE, and the members were chosen from contestants on SIXTEEN, where they competed against other JYP trainees.

Over the years the group has grown from cheerful debut-era pop into a more confident sound, and they have built a strong following in the United States as well. Several members have also gone solo, starting with Nayeon's Pop! in 2022 and Jihyo's Killin' Me Good in 2023, showing off different sides of their styles. Tzuyu followed with her own solo mini album, abouTZU, in 2024, so there is a lot to explore beyond the group releases.

To mark ten years together, TWICE released a special anniversary album, Ten: The Story Goes On, and held a 10th anniversary fan meeting for ONCE. They have also been on their THIS IS FOR world tour. Speaking to Soompi, Sana said the past ten years had gone by almost frighteningly fast, which will sound familiar to anyone who has followed them since the start.
nw-seventeen: SEVENTEEN has 13 members split into the hip-hop, vocal and performance units.
They are known for writing and choreographing much of their own work, led by members Woozi and Hoshi.
Their variety show, Going Seventeen, is a favourite way for fans to get to know them.

SEVENTEEN debuted in May 2015 under Pledis Entertainment with the mini album 17 Carat and the single Adore U. The hip-hop unit is S.Coups, Wonwoo, Mingyu and Vernon. The vocal unit is Woozi, Jeonghan, Joshua, DK and Seungkwan. The performance unit is Hoshi, Jun, The8 and Dino. Their fans are called CARAT. Pledis later became part of HYBE, and the group celebrated ten years together in 2025.

The group also splits into smaller combinations. BSS, made up of DK, Seungkwan and Hoshi, had a big hit with Fighting, and newer pairings such as CxM, with S.Coups and Mingyu, give members room to try different sounds. Singles like Very Nice, Don't Wanna Cry and God of Music show how wide the group's range is. Hoshi and Woozi have also teamed up as a pair, which makes sense given how much they shape the group's work.

Their live shows have taken them to some big stages, including the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury in 2024. They were also named UNESCO Goodwill Ambassadors for Youth. Like many Korean groups, they are working around military service, with members enlisting in turn, so fans are keeping an eye out for unit releases and full-group comebacks. Going Seventeen remains the easiest way to keep up in between.
nw-ateez: ATEEZ debuted in 2018 with a pirate concept. Their albums are linked by a story about travelling between worlds.
They are known for high-energy performances and have become one of the most successful K-Pop touring acts in the US and Europe.

ATEEZ debuted under KQ Entertainment in October 2018 with Treasure EP.1: All to Zero and the song Pirate King. The group has eight members: Hongjoong, who is the leader, Seonghwa, Yunho, Yeosang, San, Mingi, Wooyoung and Jongho. Hongjoong is also heavily involved in writing and producing their music, which is one reason their sound and story have stayed so consistent over the years.

The story runs across album series rather than single releases. The Treasure series set up the crew and their search for a lost treasure, the Zero: Fever series explored an alternate world, and The World series followed the members as they fight back against a society where passion is banned. The Golden Hour series came next, and music videos and concept films add clues that fans love to piece together.

Their success in the US has kept growing. The World EP.Fin: Will became their first number one on the Billboard 200 in 2023, followed by Golden Hour: Part.2 in 2024, and Golden Hour: Part.5 gave them a third number one in July 2026. They also performed at Coachella in 2024, and they have now had more top ten albums on the Billboard 200 than any other group this decade.
nw-batman: Batman: Year One by Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli is the classic origin. The Long Halloween is a great mystery that follows on from it.
For something modern, Scott Snyder's Court of Owls introduces a secret society that has ruled Gotham for centuries.
On screen, The Batman Part II continues Matt Reeves's detective-focused take on the character.

Batman was created by Bob Kane and Bill Finger and first appeared in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. Year One came out in 1987 in the main Batman series, and it rebuilt his early days for a new generation. The Long Halloween, by Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale, follows a killer who strikes on holidays and shows how Harvey Dent became Two-Face, so it works well as a second read.

If you enjoy those, DC's own reading guide points to a few more classics. Hush by Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee is a fast mystery that brings in a lot of Batman's allies and villains. Under the Red Hood by Judd Winick deals with the return of Jason Todd, and Batman and Son by Grant Morrison introduces Damian Wayne, Bruce's son, who later becomes Robin.

For something current, DC relaunched the main series with Batman #1 in 2025 by Matt Fraction and Jorge Jiménez, which is a clean jumping-on point. There is also Absolute Batman by Scott Snyder and Nick Dragotta, a bold new version of the character who has no fortune behind him. The Court of Owls, by Snyder and Greg Capullo, remains a fan favourite too.
nw-spider-man: Peter Parker's classic stories start with Amazing Fantasy #15 (1962). For modern readers, Ultimate Spider-Man offers a fresh start.
Miles Morales has his own series and has become just as popular, especially after the Spider-Verse films.
Spider-Gwen, Spider-Man 2099 and many others each have their own comics.

Spider-Man was created by writer Stan Lee and artist Steve Ditko, and the character's everyday problems, from paying rent to keeping up with school, were a big change for superhero comics at the time. The original Ultimate Spider-Man, launched in 2000 by Brian Michael Bendis and Mark Bagley, retold Peter's story for a new generation. The newer Ultimate Spider-Man from 2024, by Jonathan Hickman and Marco Checchetto, imagines a grown-up Peter married to Mary Jane with two children.

Miles Morales was introduced in 2011 by Brian Michael Bendis and artist Sara Pichelli, first in the Ultimate line before joining the main Marvel universe. Spider-Gwen, Gwen Stacy as a hero in her own world, debuted in Edge of Spider-Verse #2 in 2014, created by Jason Latour and Robbi Rodriguez. Spider-Man 2099, Miguel O'Hara, goes back further, to 1992, from writer Peter David and artist Rick Leonardi.

The films have given all of these heroes a much bigger audience. Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature, and Across the Spider-Verse followed in 2023, with the concluding film, Beyond the Spider-Verse, in the works. If you are new to the comics, collected editions are the easiest way in, and Marvel's digital service makes it simple to sample a few different Spider-heroes before you commit.
nw-x-men: The X-Men are mutants born with powers, led by Professor X, fighting for a world that fears them.
Classic runs like Chris Claremont's The Dark Phoenix Saga are still essential reading.
The X-Men '97 animated series brought a lot of new fans to the comics.

The X-Men were created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby and first appeared in X-Men #1 in 1963. The original team was Cyclops, Marvel Girl, Beast, Angel and Iceman. The series really took off in 1975 with Giant-Size X-Men #1 by Len Wein and Dave Cockrum, which brought in a new international line-up including Storm, Nightcrawler and Colossus, with Wolverine joining the team.

Chris Claremont then wrote the X-Men for around sixteen years, and his run with artist John Byrne produced both The Dark Phoenix Saga and Days of Future Past. For a more modern entry point, Jonathan Hickman's House of X and Powers of X from 2019 reinvented the line around the mutant island nation of Krakoa, and Marvel's own Start Here guide lists both.

On screen, the X-Men have been hugely popular since the Fox films began in 2000, with Hugh Jackman's Wolverine becoming one of the best-known superhero performances. X-Men '97, which continues the classic 1990s cartoon, was a hit on Disney+ in 2024, and a second season has been confirmed. The comics themselves have a new set of ongoing series that are easy to pick up.
nw-wonder-woman: Wonder Woman was created by William Moulton Marston and first appeared in 1941.
George Pérez's 1987 run rebuilt her mythology and is often called the definitive version.
Greg Rucka's Rebirth run is a great modern starting point.

Marston created Diana with artist Harry G. Peter, and she debuted in All Star Comics #8 before headlining Sensation Comics and then her own title. She is one of DC's big three alongside Superman and Batman, and she has been published almost continuously since the 1940s, which few characters of any kind can claim. Marston, a psychologist, wanted a hero who won through strength and compassion rather than fists alone, and that idea is still at the heart of the character today.

Pérez's relaunch came straight after Crisis on Infinite Earths. It reshaped Diana around Greek myth, with the gods of Olympus, Themyscira and villains such as Cheetah and Ares playing central roles. Greg Potter and Len Wein co-wrote the early issues. Rucka's Rebirth run alternated between two stories, The Lies with art by Liam Sharp and Year One with art by Nicola Scott.

Other runs worth reading include Gail Simone's late 2000s stories, Brian Azzarello and Cliff Chiang's New 52 run from 2011, and Absolute Wonder Woman by Kelly Thompson and Hayden Sherman. On screen, Gal Gadot played Diana in Patty Jenkins's 2017 film, and DC Studios has announced Paradise Lost, a series set on Themyscira. There is plenty to choose from depending on the tone you like.
nw-black-panther: Black Panther first appeared in Fantastic Four #52 in 1966. He was the first Black superhero in mainstream American comics.
Christopher Priest's run turned him into a master strategist, and Ta-Nehisi Coates later explored Wakanda's politics.
The films brought Wakanda's vibranium-powered world to a global audience.

T'Challa was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. In his very first story, he invites the Fantastic Four to Wakanda and beats them one by one, then teams up with them against the villain Ulysses Klaw. It was a strong introduction that showed him as a king, a scientist and a fighter at once. He joined the Avengers soon afterwards and has been a key part of the Marvel universe ever since.

Wakanda's power comes from vibranium, a rare metal found only there, which made the nation the most advanced in the world while staying hidden. Don McGregor's Panther's Rage storyline in Jungle Action during the 1970s is often called one of the first long-form graphic novels in superhero comics. Later, Reginald Hudlin's run had Shuri, T'Challa's sister, take up the Black Panther title herself.

Ryan Coogler's Black Panther in 2018, starring Chadwick Boseman, became the first superhero film nominated for the Oscar for Best Picture and won three Academy Awards. Its sequel, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, followed in 2022 after Boseman's death, with Letitia Wright's Shuri stepping forward. The animated series Eyes of Wakanda arrived on Disney+ in 2025, looking at Wakandan warriors throughout history.
nw-one-piece-manga: One Piece has been published weekly in Shonen Jump since 1997 and has sold more copies than any other manga series.
The final saga began after the Wano arc, and Oda has said he is heading toward the ending.
Chapters are released in English on the same day as Japan through official apps.

Eiichiro Oda started One Piece in Weekly Shonen Jump in July 1997, after working as an assistant on other Jump series. The story follows Monkey D. Luffy, a boy whose body turned to rubber after eating a Devil Fruit, as he gathers a crew and sails the Grand Line to find the treasure called the One Piece and become King of the Pirates.

In 2022 Oda took a month off to prepare for the final saga, during a busy summer that included the manga's 25th anniversary and the film One Piece Film Red. By then the series had more than 490 million copies in circulation worldwide. It also holds a Guinness World Record for the most copies published for the same comic book series by a single author.

The anime has been made by Toei Animation since 1999, and Netflix's live-action series has brought in plenty of new fans too. In English, VIZ Media publishes the collected volumes, and Shueisha's Manga Plus app carries new chapters at the same time as Japan. Oda has been clear that the ending is on its way, so this is a great time to catch up.
nw-dragon-ball: Dragon Ball follows Goku from a kid searching for the Dragon Balls to the strongest fighter in the universe.
Akira Toriyama passed away in 2024, and fans around the world shared tributes to his work.
Dragon Ball Super and the Daima anime continue the story.

Dragon Ball ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 1984 to 1995 and was collected in 42 volumes. Before it, Toriyama was already famous for the comedy manga Dr. Slump, and alongside his manga work he designed the characters and monsters for the Dragon Quest games and worked on the characters for Chrono Trigger. His clean, playful art style is recognisable at a glance, even to people who have never read a single chapter.

The anime is made by Toei Animation, with Dragon Ball Z following the original series in 1989. In Japan, Masako Nozawa has voiced Goku since the very first episode in 1986. The series' influence is easy to spot: creators such as Eiichiro Oda of One Piece and Masashi Kishimoto of Naruto grew up reading it, and training arcs, power levels and huge tournament battles became staples of the genre.

Toriyama stayed involved right to the end. He worked on the story and character designs for Dragon Ball Daima, which premiered in October 2024, after his death that March. The Dragon Ball Super manga continues with artist Toyotarou, who worked closely with Toriyama for years. There are games too, including Dragon Ball: Sparking! Zero, so there are plenty of ways to keep enjoying the world he built.
nw-superman: Superman first appeared in Action Comics #1 in 1938, created by writer Jerry Siegel and artist Joe Shuster. Almost every superhero since has borrowed something from him.

All-Star Superman by Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely is the most recommended starting point: twelve issues that capture everything good about the character. Superman: Birthright and Superman for All Seasons are great takes on his early years.
The 2025 Superman film by James Gunn, starring David Corenswet, brought a lot of new readers to the comics, and DC's current Superman series is a friendly place to start reading monthly.

Siegel and Shuster were two young men from Cleveland, and they sold Superman to the company that became DC. Within a couple of years he had his own comic, a newspaper strip and a radio show. Many of the things we now think of as part of the character, like kryptonite and the Daily Planet, were added over those early years rather than in the first issue.

Beyond the usual favourites, DC's own list for new readers also points to Superman: Red Son by Mark Millar, which imagines Superman landing in the Soviet Union, and Superman: Secret Identity by Kurt Busiek and Stuart Immonen, about a boy in our world who wakes up with Superman's powers. For the Man Who Has Everything by Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons is a great single-issue read.

The 2025 film also starred Rachel Brosnahan as Lois Lane and Nicholas Hoult as Lex Luthor, and it launched the new DC Universe led by James Gunn and Peter Safran. Supergirl, starring Milly Alcock, followed in 2026, and Gunn has announced a follow-up called Man of Tomorrow, so there is plenty for new fans to look forward to, whether you start with the films or the comics.
nw-jujutsu-kaisen-manga: Gege Akutami's Jujutsu Kaisen ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2018 until its final chapter in 2024, collected in 30 volumes.
The anime is still adapting the later arcs, so the manga is the only place to read the ending of the Culling Game and the final fight with Sukuna.
If you have watched up to the Shibuya Incident, pick the manga up from around volume 17.

The series grew out of a short prequel Akutami wrote in 2017, later collected as Jujutsu Kaisen 0, which introduces Yuta Okkotsu and Gojo as a teacher. The main story launched in March 2018 and finished with chapter 271 on 30 September 2024, after around six and a half years. Viz Media publishes the English edition, and Shueisha's MANGA Plus carries it digitally.

The anime is made by MAPPA. Sunghoo Park directed the first season in 2020 and the Jujutsu Kaisen 0 film, and Shota Goshozono took over for the second season in 2023, which covered Gojo's Past and the Shibuya Incident. MAPPA has since moved on to the Culling Game arc, which means anime-only fans are heading into some of the story's wildest fights.

The ending is not quite the end of the world. Akutami returned as writer on Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo, a short spin-off drawn by Yuji Iwasaki, which began in Weekly Shonen Jump in 2025 and is set decades after the main story. It is a good thing to pick up once you have finished the last volume. You will spot a few familiar names along the way.
nw-solo-leveling-manga: Solo Leveling started as a web novel by Chugong. The webtoon, drawn by DUBU of Redice Studio, turned it into a global hit with its full-colour action pages.
The main story finished in 2021, and a side story and a sequel series have followed.
Reading on a phone suits the vertical scroll format, and the big fights feel like they were made for it.

Chugong's web novel first appeared on KakaoPage in 2016, and the webtoon ran there from March 2018 to December 2021. It follows Sung Jinwoo, known as the weakest hunter of all mankind, who gets a strange system that lets him level up like a game character. Sadly, DUBU, whose real name was Jang Sung-rak, died in July 2022, and fans around the world paid tribute to his artwork.

The anime is made by A-1 Pictures, with music by Hiroyuki Sawano, and the first season aired in January 2024. The second season, subtitled Arise from the Shadow, followed in January 2025. The anime covers the story up to the middle of the webtoon, so readers can jump into the webtoon to find out how Jinwoo's battle with the Monarchs ends, including the big final confrontation.

The sequel, Solo Leveling: Ragnarok, started in August 2024 and follows Jinwoo's son, Sung Suho. It is written by Chugong and drawn by JIN, also from Redice Studio. There is also Solo Leveling: Arise, an action game from Netmarble released in 2024. In English, Yen Press publishes the original webtoon and novels in print, so collectors can have the whole story on their shelves too.
nw-demon-slayer-manga: Koyoharu Gotouge's manga ran from 2016 to 2020 in Weekly Shonen Jump and became one of the best-selling manga series ever.
The Infinity Castle arc, now being adapted as a trilogy of films, starts around volume 16.
The final volumes include an epilogue that surprised a lot of readers, so try to avoid spoilers until you get there.

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba follows Tanjiro Kamado, a boy in Taisho-era Japan whose family is killed by a demon and whose sister Nezuko is turned into one. He joins the Demon Slayer Corps to find a cure for her and to track down Muzan Kibutsuji, the first demon. The series runs to 205 chapters, and it was Gotouge's first long-running serialisation.

The manga's final chapter ran in Weekly Shonen Jump in May 2020. At that point the franchise already had more than 60 million copies in circulation, a huge jump helped by the success of ufotable's anime in 2019. Sales kept climbing after that, especially once the Mugen Train film became the highest-grossing film ever released in Japan, a record it still holds today.

In English, VIZ Media publishes the full series in 23 volumes, and there are also box sets if you want to read it all at once. After the main story ended, a short spinoff about the Flame Hashira, Rengoku Gaiden, was written by Ryoji Hirano, and it is a nice extra for anyone who loved Rengoku in the Mugen Train arc.
nw-black-clover: Yuki Tabata's Black Clover started in Weekly Shonen Jump in 2015. In 2023 it moved to Jump GIGA, releasing longer chapters less often.
The story is in its final arc, with Asta and Yuno both closing in on their dream of becoming the Wizard King.
The anime ended at the Spade Kingdom arc, and the Sword of the Wizard King film is a side story, so the manga is where the main plot continues.

Black Clover follows Asta, an orphan born with no magic at all in a world where magic is everything, and his rival Yuno, who is one of the most gifted mages of his generation. Asta makes up for it with relentless training and his anti-magic swords, and he joins the Black Bulls, a squad of misfits led by Yami Sukehiro. It is a classic Jump story about hard work and friendship, told with plenty of heart.

When Tabata moved the series to Jump GIGA, he said the quarterly magazine would be a better fit for his personal situation as a writer. The final arc then built towards its climax over the next few years, and in May 2026 the manga reached its ending in Jump GIGA, after more than eleven years of serialisation. So if you have been waiting to read the whole thing in one go, now is the moment.

The anime is also coming back. Studio Pierrot, which made all 170 episodes of the original series between October 2017 and March 2021, is returning for a new season that has been announced for 2026, with Crunchyroll streaming it. In Japanese, Asta is voiced by Gakuto Kajiwara, whose very loud performance fans either adore or find hilarious. Either way, it will be good to hear it again.
nw-hunger-games: The Hunger Games franchise started with Suzanne Collins's 2008 novel and grew into one of the biggest young-adult film series, starring Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss Everdeen.

The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (2023) went back 64 years to show a young Coriolanus Snow. The next prequel, Sunrise on the Reaping, adapts Collins's 2025 novel about Haymitch Abernathy's time in the 50th Games, the Second Quarter Quell.
If you are new to Panem, start with the original four films before the prequels. They make the twists in the newer stories hit much harder.

Collins followed the first novel with Catching Fire and Mockingjay, and the films ran from 2012 to 2015, with Mockingjay split into two parts. Gary Ross directed the first film, and Francis Lawrence took over from Catching Fire onwards. Josh Hutcherson and Liam Hemsworth played Peeta and Gale, and the series made more than three billion dollars at the box office.

Francis Lawrence also directed The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, which starred Tom Blyth as Snow and Rachel Zegler as Lucy Gray Baird. He is back again for Sunrise on the Reaping, working from a screenplay by Billy Ray, with Nina Jacobson and Brad Simpson producing for Color Force as they have on every film in the series. Lionsgate has released the films from the start.

The film is due in cinemas on 20 November 2026. Joseph Zada plays the young Haymitch and Whitney Peak plays his girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird. The cast also includes Ralph Fiennes as President Snow, Jesse Plemons as a young Plutarch Heavensbee, Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket and Kieran Culkin as Caesar Flickerman, so fans of the originals will spot plenty of familiar names.
nw-fortnite: Fortnite started life as Save the World, a co-op mode about building forts against zombie-like husks. In September 2017 Epic Games added Battle Royale and made it free to play, and within months it was one of the biggest games on the planet.

The idea is simple: up to 100 players drop from the Battle Bus onto an island, grab weapons and fight until one player or squad is left while a storm shrinks the map. What made Fortnite different was building, letting players throw up walls, ramps and towers in seconds.
If building feels overwhelming, Zero Build mode removes it completely, so you can learn the map and the weapons first. Many players never go back.

Fortnite has also become famous for crossovers. Characters from Marvel, Star Wars, Dragon Ball, Street Fighter and many other series have appeared as outfits, and big in-game live events, from concerts to story finales, have drawn huge crowds of players at the same moment.

Beyond Battle Royale, the game now includes LEGO Fortnite, Rocket Racing and Fortnite Festival, a rhythm mode where you play along to real songs. Creators can also build their own islands with Unreal Editor for Fortnite, so there is always something new to jump into.

It runs on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch and mobile, with cross-play and cross-progression, so you can pick up where you left off on almost any device. For a free game, it is hard to think of a better place to start with online shooters.
nw-my-hero-academia-manga: My Hero Academia ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from July 2014 to August 2024 and is collected in 42 volumes, so the whole story is out and ready to read.
It follows Izuku Midoriya, a boy born without a Quirk in a world where almost everyone has one, who inherits the power One For All from the hero All Might.
Horikoshi's love of American superhero comics shows in every page, from the hero agencies to the costume designs, and his big two-page spreads are a highlight.
In English the series is published by VIZ Media, and new readers can try the opening chapters for free on the Shonen Jump app and MANGA Plus.
The final volume includes extra pages that continue after the last chapter, which fans say gives the class a proper farewell.
If you have watched the anime, reading from Volume 1 is still worth it: the manga moves faster and includes small moments the adaptation had to trim.
